canonical_name: Weak maximum principle for the heat equation
canonical_statement: Let U be a bounded open subset of a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and T > 0. If u is continuous on the closure of U x [0,T], is twice continuously differentiable in space and once continuously differentiable in time on U x (0,T], and satisfies u_t - Delta u = 0 there, then the maximum of u on the closed space-time cylinder equals its maximum on the parabolic boundary (the initial face together with the lateral boundary).
domain_and_universes: Provisional: n : Nat, U : Set (EuclideanSpace Real (Fin n)), T : Real, u : EuclideanSpace Real (Fin n) -> Real -> Real; exact Lean universes and analytic predicates remain for the statement phase.
quantifiers: U : bounded open subset of EuclideanSpace Real (Fin n)
u : closure(U x [0,T]) -> Real, represented by a suitably regular ambient function
hypotheses: u is continuous on the closed cylinder
u has the spatial C2 and temporal C1 regularity needed on U x (0,T]
partial_t u - Laplacian_x u = 0 on U x (0,T]
conclusion: max_{closure(U) x [0,T]} u = max_{(closure(U) x {0}) union (frontier(U) x [0,T])} u

alternate_encodings.target: supremum inequality u(x,t) <= sup on the parabolic boundary
subsolution form partial_t u - Laplacian u <= 0
alternate_encodings.relationship: strictly more general weak maximum principle

alternate_encodings.target: strong maximum principle for an interior maximum

included_boundary_cases: The initial face t = 0 and lateral boundary frontier(U) x [0,T] form the parabolic boundary. The terminal interior face U x {T} belongs to the cylinder, not to the parabolic boundary.
excluded_degenerate_cases: T = 0, unbounded spatial domains, weak/distributional solutions, nonhomogeneous equations, and strong-principle equality cases are outside this root.
